output.title: Focus blocks come after the workflow decision
output.body:
Before you protect a focus block, decide what is actually stealing the time.

For an owner-operator, the useful question is not whether AI sounds smart. It is whether one recurring task keeps interrupting the week: repeated customer questions, invoice data entry, or lead follow-up. If the work changes every time, it is probably not the first thing to automate. If it follows a pattern, that is a workflow worth looking at.

A plain test is enough: does the task repeat weekly, and does it have a clear input and output? If yes, note it for a week before you try to make room for automation. If no, keep it manual and move on. No spreadsheet heroics required; a week of notes usually tells you more than a hunch with a decent keyboard.

That is the bounded decision Bareni starts with: identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and if it does, define a pilot scope. That sequence is intended as an operating practice, not a guarantee, and final approval stays with the owner.

The practical next step is simple: name the one task, time how often it interrupts your week, and check whether it repeats in a pattern before you protect the block.
